rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.read: Most central banks still lean toward higher rates because energy keeps inflation high, and this week Australia and Britain are both expected to raise them. With those hikes mostly priced, their currencies will move on whether the banks hint at more. In the US, bets on a December Fed hike held firm.
rows.figure: RBA Nov 3 hike to 4.85% ~81–90%; BoE Nov 5 hike to 4.00% ~94%; Fed Dec hike ~72–75% (from ~70% Oct 30); ECB Dec ~86%; BoJ Dec ~80%; BoC Dec ~45%; RBNZ Dec ~75%

rows.title: Growth
rows.read: China sent mixed signals: the official factory survey slipped into decline, but a private survey of smaller firms stayed solid. That leaves Australia and New Zealand without a clear push either way. US factory figures later today give the first look at how the US economy began the autumn quarter.
rows.figure: China official manufacturing PMI 49.3 (poll 50.0); RatingDog PMI 52.0 (poll 51.6); US ISM manufacturing today, forecast 54.5

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: Cheaper oil overnight eased some of the fear that energy will keep pushing prices up. But inflation is still well above target in the US, the euro area, Britain and Australia, so central banks have little room to relax. Euro-area figures on Wednesday are the week's main inflation test.
rows.figure: Euro-area flash HICP Nov 4: forecast 4.0% (Sep 3.8%), core 2.5%; Swiss CPI Nov 3: forecast 0.0% m/m; Brent ~$110 (−3%)

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.read: Markets started November calmer after October's tech share slide, and the weekend passed without a US strike on Iran. That cut demand for the safe-haven yen and franc. Attacks on Gulf shipping continue, so the calm could break quickly.
rows.figure: USD/JPY ~157.8 (+0.2%); USD/CHF ~0.824; gold ~$3,907 (+0.6%); ~10 Gulf shipping incidents in three days

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.read: Oil fell as talks in Qatar raised hopes of ending the US–Iran war. That trims the boost oil exporters like Canada get, and eases the cost for importers like Japan and the euro area. Prices are still high by historical standards, so the gap between winners and losers remains.
rows.figure: Brent ~$109.8 (−3.2%), WTI ~$100.5 (−3.5%); OPEC+ December targets unchanged

rows.title: Positioning
rows.read: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the Canadian dollar, and cheaper oil now takes some pressure off those bets. They are also betting against the euro and the kiwi, while real money investors bet for the euro. Their large bets on gold are shrinking, and their bets on oil rising are among the weakest in a decade.
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 27: funds strongly against CAD (added), against EUR (real money for), against NZD (sharply added), for AUD (real money strongly against), strongly for gold (cut); oil net long among weakest since 2015

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.read: Fitch joined Moody's in putting France's credit rating on negative outlook, which keeps a weight on the euro. France's parliament votes on the revenue side of its budget on Tuesday. Canada presents its budget on Thursday.
